item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Wed Aug 12, 4:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Yolo County Fair — Wed Aug 12, 5:00 PM — Yolo County Fairgrounds
item.description: Yolo County Fair August 7th-9th & August 12th-16th The Yolo County Fair, California’s longest-running free-gate fair, returns in 2026 with more days, more entertainment and more opportunities for families to celebrate the region’s agricultural heritage. For the first time in its history, the Fair will span eight days over two weekends. An Outdoor Kickoff Weekend will run Friday, Aug. 7 through Sunday, Aug. 9, followed by the traditional Fair Wednesday, Aug. 12 through Sunday, Aug. 16. Admission to the Fair, themed “Hog August Nights this year,” remains free. The new opening weekend will feature headline arena concerts by country music stars Hunter Hayes and Chris Lane, corgi racing, livestock shows, a carnival midway, silent discos and live entertainment on multiple stages. item.description:
Pence Adult Art Programs The Pence’s 6-session Healing Arts workshop uses art as a healing language for those experiencing grief from the loss of a loved one. Through the process of art making, participants will have opportunities for discussion, education, and connecting with peers in a safe and supportive space in the Pence Learning Center under the guidance of facilitators Amy Vidra and Lyndsey Rocca.
REGISTRATION ONLINE IS REQUIRED IN ADVANCE through the Pence Gallery's website, and space is limited to the first 8 participants who register. Participants must be 18 or older, and no art experience is necessary. This program is generously sponsored by Bob & Joanne Andresen.
Healing Arts 6-Session Workshop Fridays\, 10\-11:45 AM \| Oct\. 9\, 16\, 23\, 30 & Nov\. 6\, 13 $25 Members, $35 Non-Members (all materials included)

item.title: Susannah Israel: Procession — Wed Aug 12 — John Natsoulas Gallery
item.description: The John Natsoulas Gallery is thrilled to announce the exhibition of Susannah Israel’s distinctive ceramics. Her individualized figures each possess an openness of expression, inviting close contemplation and investigation into their stories. To be exhibited on the second floor of the gallery, her body of work is a reflection of the humor she uses to confront the struggles of life. Her emphasis of gesture takes an equal role to her interest in abstraction and distortion. The dynamic figures, some in conversation with a paired piece, offer viewers discrete narratives to consider, even as the overarching themes remain cohesive. The wide date-range present in this exhibition provides insight into her developments. Her repetitious use of unglazed terracotta-colored clay reminds viewers of the earthen and historical origins of her medium. The warmth and rich coloration of each figure shines, even when the figure is subsumed entirely with glazes and surface designs. Originally from New Yor

item.title: Woody De Othello: coming forth by day — Wed Aug 12 — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This solo exhibition by the Oakland-based artist featuring a new series of works that explore the primordial relationship between body, earth and spirit. Othello honors an important Northern California lineage of ceramic artists and expands that tradition by drawing on knowledge and philosophies from around the world through a decolonial lens. Through material experimentation and sculptural gesture, the exhibition considers how objects carry history, absorb meaning and serve as vessels for both spiritual and emotional experience. “Woody De Othello: coming forth by day” is organized by Pérez Art Museum Miami. The Manetti Shrem Museum presentation is organized by Susie Kantor, associate curator and exhibition department head. Open 10am – 5pm, Wednesday through Saturday. Click here for holiday hours.
Source: The Dirt

item.description:

Every Wednesday evening through August 26, the market expands to 4:00 – 8:00 PM, turning Central Park into the perfect spot for a relaxed picnic dinner. Shop fresh produce, artisan goods, and a wide variety of prepared foods from your favorite vendors. Enjoy local craft beer, wine, and brand new this year – mead! Each week features live music and children’s activities, creating a festive, family-friendly atmosphere. Bring blankets, lawn chairs, and reusable bags. item.title: Intermediate Watercolor with Misuk Goltz (5-sessions) — Tue Sep 1, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Pence Adult Art Programs This 5-week workshop with Misuk Goltz will focus on using your brushes to their full potential and practicing diverse hand motions to achieve painterly, expressive watercolor paintings. Students will learn how to distribute different values to create balanced and sophisticated artwork while painting various subjects. Please note that this class is intended for participants who have previous experience with watercolor techniques and color blending. The use of high-quality watercolor materials is strongly recommended to achieve the best results.
Intermediate Watercolor with Misuk Goltz Tuesdays\, 10 AM \- 12 PM \| September 1\, 8\, 15\, 22\, 29 $170 Members, $190 Non-Members (Materials not included)
**Registration is required through the [Pence's website (CLICK HERE)](https://pencegallery.org/education/programs/workshops-and-classes/).**
Any questions? Email pencegallery@gmail.com.
Source: Meetup: Pence Art Programs

item.title: Davis City Council Meetings — Thu Nov 5, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change.
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance.
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: DJUSD Board Meetings — Thu Nov 5, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
DJUSD Board meetings offer insight on how the school district remains responsive to the community’s values, beliefs, and priorities. The Board meetings occur on every first and third Thursday, in the City of Davis Community Chambers. 23 Russell Boulevard. Public session starts at 6:30 PM. Meetings are cablecast live on Channel 17 (Comcast) or streamed on the DJUSD-TV website.
The Davis Joint Unified School District’s Board of Education is comprised of five community members, responsible for setting district policy, approving the budget, and hiring the superintendent for schools in Davis, California. The agendas for the meetings are posted at least 72 hours in advance.
For more information on special meetings, agendas, public comment, and more, visit the DJUSD Board site.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Aug 26, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: Picnic in the Park at Davis Farmers Market – Wednesday Evenings (50th Anniversary Year) — Wed Oct 21, 4:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
The beloved Picnic in the Park season is back at the Davis Farmers Market starting Wednesday, April 1, 2026! Every Wednesday evening through August 26, the market expands to 4:00 – 8:00 PM, turning Central Park into the perfect spot for a relaxed picnic dinner. Shop fresh produce, artisan goods, and a wide variety of prepared foods from your favorite vendors. Enjoy local craft beer, wine, and brand new this year – mead! Each week features live music and children’s activities, creating a festive, family-friendly atmosphere. Bring blankets, lawn chairs, and reusable bags. It’s the ideal way to unwind, connect with neighbors, and support local farmers and food makers. This year is extra special as the Davis Farmers Market celebrates its 50th Anniversary! Don’t miss the big anniversary celebration on Saturday, August 1, 2026. New in 2026: The Market Memories Cookbook (presale now at davis-farmers-market). Highlights Include:
